_about: AgeWell AI & Safety Notes. Single source for the homepage cards, notes.html and Ask Mae. Publication is manual: a person writes each note, checks it against the official source, sets reviewed, then runs python3 _tools/build-pages.py. Nothing is fetched or posted automatically. founderText keeps the founder-approved wording verbatim; the other fields split that same wording into company statement vs AgeWell guidance.

notes.title: AI can sometimes take unexpected actions

company.name: Anthropic
company.summary: Anthropic reported unintended actions observed during testing and internal use, including real form submissions. The company described limited impact.

notes.status: This is a research disclosure, not an announcement of a new consumer feature.
notes.step: Review connected permissions and check actions before submission.
notes.limitations: The findings do not establish how often this happens in everyday consumer use.
notes.teaching: Mae can prepare the form. Mable presses Submit.

source.title: Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use

founderText: Anthropic reported unintended actions observed during testing and internal use, including real form submissions. The company described limited impact; the findings do not establish how often this happens in everyday consumer use.
For anyone using AI assistants: review connected permissions and check actions before submission. This is a research disclosure, not an announcement of a new consumer feature.

notes.title: AI glasses show accessibility potential

company.name: Meta
company.summary: Meta announced a donation of 1,000 AI glasses to Singapore community organizations, alongside funding for accessibility training.

notes.affects: Older adults with low vision, and caregivers.
notes.step: Explore supported demonstrations and training before deciding whether these tools fit daily needs.
notes.limitations: It does not establish a free U.S. program or an individual delivery date.
notes.guidance: Check important AI descriptions independently and continue using established mobility supports.
notes.teaching: Useful technology starts with useful training.

source.title: Meta Donates 1,000 AI Glasses to Singapore’s Disability Community

founderText: Meta announced a donation of 1,000 AI glasses to Singapore community organizations, alongside funding for accessibility training. The announcement concerns Singapore partners; it does not establish a free U.S. program or an individual delivery date.
For older adults with low vision and caregivers: explore supported demonstrations and training before deciding whether these tools fit daily needs.
